preamble: Diphthongization of a mid front vowel /e/ to [ei] through development of a palatal off-glide. It is common in the history of European languages: Latin tonic ē in open syllables became Old French ei, Early Modern English /eː/ became Modern English /eɪ/, and Icelandic diphthongized e before ng and nk.

examples.note: Tonic close-mid e in a free syllable diphthongized to ei (later oi: toile).
Early Old French and northern form; later mois.
The 16th–17th-century long /eː/ (from Middle English /aː/ via the Great Vowel Shift) diphthongized to Modern English /eɪ/; also great, steak.
Icelandic e diphthongizes to ei before ng and nk.
